note: Scores are 0-3 expert judgements. `evidence` lists supporting literature for the model entry; `notes` maps an area or requirement key to a one-line rationale or source. Citations were added by the maintainer and should be verified (see docs/EXPERT_REVIEW.md).

models.name: In silico: QSAR, PBPK and connectome models
models.status: Not regulated under ASPA. No animals.
models.strengths: Fast, cheap, unlimited conditions. PBPK can predict human exposure; whole-brain connectome models (for example the FlyWire Drosophila brain) can generate circuit hypotheses before any experiment.
models.limits: Only as good as the data behind it. Usually needs experimental validation.
evidence: Jones HM, Rowland-Yeo K (2013) Basic concepts in physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling in drug discovery and development. CPT: Pharmacometrics & Systems Pharmacology 2: e63.
Dorkenwald S et al. (2024) Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain. Nature 634: 124-138.

models.name: Human cell lines and primary cells (2D)
models.status: Not regulated under ASPA. Human material may need consent and HTA-compliant handling.
models.strengths: Human, reproducible, high throughput. Primary immune cells such as PBMCs give donor-relevant responses.
models.limits: Lose tissue architecture and much of their differentiated function in 2D.
models.bankable: Yes. Routine cryopreservation; assay-ready frozen monolayers remove repeat culture (Tomas et al., Biomacromolecules 2022).
evidence: Tomas RMF, Bissoyi A, Congdon TR, Gibson MI (2022) Assay-ready cryopreserved cell monolayers enabled by macromolecular cryoprotectants. Biomacromolecules 23: 3948.

models.name: 3D liver spheroids
models.strengths: Keep liver function and drug metabolism for weeks, and suit repeat-dose toxicity better than 2D culture.
models.limits: Single organ, no blood flow or systemic exposure.
models.bankable: Yes. Spheroids can be cryopreserved with macromolecular cryoprotectants and used straight from the freezer (Bissoyi et al., ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2023).
evidence: Bell CC et al. (2016) Characterization of primary human hepatocyte spheroids as a model system for drug-induced liver injury, liver function and disease. Scientific Reports 6: 25187.
Bissoyi A et al. (2023) Cryopreservation of liver-cell spheroids with macromolecular cryoprotectants. ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces 15: 2630.

models.name: Intestinal Transwell barrier models (Caco-2 / HT29-MTX)
models.strengths: Measure permeability, TEER and tight junctions; widely used to predict intestinal absorption.
models.limits: Normally take about three weeks to differentiate; lack the full cell diversity of the gut.
models.bankable: Yes. Differentiated barriers frozen on the Transwell recover function in about 7 days instead of 21 (Bissoyi et al., ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2024).
evidence: Bissoyi A et al. (2024) Cryopreservation and rapid recovery of differentiated intestinal epithelial barrier cells at complex Transwell interfaces. ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces 16: 23027.

models.name: Organoids (iPSC or adult stem cell derived)
models.status: Not regulated under ASPA. Matrigel and some reagents are animal-derived; consider animal-free matrices.
models.strengths: Self-organising human tissue with several cell types; patient-specific disease models.
models.limits: Variable between batches; immature compared with adult tissue; no vasculature.
models.bankable: Partly. Organoids can be cryopreserved, but recovery varies by type.
evidence: Lancaster MA, Knoblich JA (2014) Organogenesis in a dish: modeling development and disease using organoid technologies. Science 345: 1247125.

models.name: Organ-on-chip and microphysiological systems
models.strengths: Add flow, mechanical forces and links between organ compartments; some multi-organ chips model systemic exposure.
models.limits: Lower throughput, specialist equipment, still being validated for regulatory use.
models.bankable: Limited. Banking pre-built chips is an open problem.
evidence: Ewart L et al. (2022) Performance assessment and economic analysis of a human Liver-Chip for predictive toxicology. Communications Medicine 2: 154.

models.name: Drosophila melanogaster (fruit fly)
models.strengths: Whole organism with behaviour and powerful genetics; about 75 percent of human disease genes have a fly counterpart. A complete adult brain connectome (FlyWire, 2024) makes circuit questions tractable.
models.limits: Not a vertebrate: limited for mammalian physiology, adaptive immunity and PK.
models.bankable: Emerging. Embryo vitrification lets fly lines be stored frozen instead of maintained as live stocks.
evidence: Ugur B, Chen K, Bellen HJ (2016) Drosophila tools and assays for the study of human diseases. Disease Models & Mechanisms 9: 235-244.
Dorkenwald S et al. (2024) Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain. Nature 634: 124-138.

models.name: C. elegans (nematode)
models.strengths: Tiny, fast, fully mapped nervous system and cell lineage; very high throughput.
evidence: Corsi AK, Wightman B, Chalfie M (2015) A transparent window into biology: a primer on Caenorhabditis elegans. Genetics 200: 387-407.

models.name: Zebrafish larvae before independent feeding
models.status: Not protected under ASPA until capable of independent feeding (about 5 days post-fertilisation at 28.5 C). Older fish are protected.
models.strengths: Vertebrate organism, transparent, high throughput; established for developmental toxicity screening.
models.limits: Short non-protected window; work beyond it needs licences.
models.bankable: Partly. Sperm cryopreservation is routine; embryos are not.
evidence: OECD (2013) Test No. 236: Fish Embryo Acute Toxicity (FET) Test. OECD Guidelines for the Testing of Chemicals, Section 2.

models.name: Ex vivo tissue (precision-cut slices, explants)
models.status: Uses tissue from animals or humans. Tissue shared from animals already killed for other studies avoids extra animals.
models.strengths: Keeps the native architecture and every cell type of the tissue; one animal or donor gives many slices.
models.bankable: Partly. Cryopreserved slices and tissue banks extend use of each donor.
evidence: de Graaf IAM et al. (2010) Preparation and incubation of precision-cut liver and intestinal slices for application in drug metabolism and toxicity studies. Nature Protocols 5: 1540-1551.

models.name: Rodents (mice, rats)
models.status: Protected under ASPA. Needs establishment, project and personal licences, ethical review and full application of the 3Rs.
models.strengths: Whole mammalian physiology, systemic exposure, adaptive immunity and complex behaviour.
models.limits: Ethical cost; species differences from humans; lower throughput and higher cost.
models.bankable: Yes. Embryo and sperm cryopreservation lets lines be archived instead of bred continuously.
evidence: Percie du Sert N et al. (2020) The ARRIVE guidelines 2.0: updated guidelines for reporting animal research. PLoS Biology 18: e3000410.
